title: WeirdChat (transluce, 2026-07-21)
abstract:
Corpus sentences naming Bloom (system-card corpus docs.sqlite, document slug in brackets):
[transluce-deepseek-v4-flash-independent-eval] To score prompts with log-prob access, we used the PRBO, a method we previously introduced that estimates how close a prompt is to triggering a behavior. - Generating a large volume of prompts with Bloom.
[transluce-deepseek-v4-flash-independent-eval] Bloom uses an LLM to generate candidate prompts directly from the behavior description, with no further optimization.
[transluce-deepseek-v4-flash-independent-eval] Even though Bloom is black-box, we found that running it at scale (e.g. using over 100,000 samples) can often surface difficult behaviors.
[transluce-deepseek-v4-flash-independent-eval] Bloom We made the following changes to Bloom to adapt it to our setting.
[transluce-deepseek-v4-flash-independent-eval] Bloom normally has the evaluator conduct a multi-turn conversation with the subject model where it provides a system prompt; we rewrote the rollout prompt so the evaluator generates exactly one standalone user message.
[transluce-deepseek-v4-flash-independent-eval] To reduce costs, we use Gemma 4 31B as the evaluator model at each stage of the pipeline.
[transluce-deepseek-v4-flash-independent-eval] For each behavior, we run Bloom with a budget of 100,000-500,000 rollouts, and scenario ideation is done in independent batches of 50 per evaluator call.
